sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 20 students, 8 preferred pizza. Based on this sample, about how many of the 200 students in the school would you expect to prefer pizza?

steps: Find the sample proportion: 8 out of 20 preferred pizza.
Scale up to the population: the school is 200 ÷ 20 = 10 times the sample size.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 16, 15, 17, 11, 11. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 1033 commuters on a train line. Student A takes a random sample of 48. Student B takes a random sample of 16. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Student B's sample of 16, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Student A's sample of 48, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.
Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.

items.prompt: A student surveys 79 students at Lincoln Middle School using a convenience sample of her classmates only and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 3239 students at Lincoln Middle School?
choices: Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.

items.prompt: A sample of 7 values is: 38, 40, 37, 20, 9, 31, 9. What is the mean of this data set?
A data set has 6 values: 26, 29, 32, 27, 31, 31. What is the new mean if an outlier of 87 is added to the data set, making 7 values in all?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A data set is: 48, 20, 40, 33, 29, with a mean of 34. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two data sets have means of 60 and 83. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 7. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Sample A: 55, 30, 54, 55, 49, 21. Sample B: 58, 45, 55, 52, 65, 79. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
